title: The BlackRock Foundation commits €15 million over five years to power the next generation of skilled trades workers in Germany
summary: The BlackRock Foundation commits €15 million over five years to power the next generation of skilled trades workers in Germany
body_markdown:
*New BlackRock Future Builders™ Germany initiative will help more than 5,000 people pursue high-demand skilled trades careers*


*BlackRock will partner with JOBLINGE and the Senior Expert Service, two longstanding organizations working alongside employers, training providers and apprentices within Germany’s world-leading vocational training system*


**FRANKFURT, 19 October 2026** - BlackRock today announced a €15 million philanthropic commitment over five years to expand economic opportunity and help power Germany’s next generation of skilled trades workers through BlackRock Future Builders, an initiative funded by The BlackRock Foundation.


BlackRock Future Builders will help address Germany’s skilled trades shortage by connecting more people to high-demand apprenticeships and providing the support needed to complete them successfully. As the first European expansion of the global BlackRock Future Builders initiative, the program in Germany will build on the strengths of the country’s world-leading vocational training system and work through established national organizations.


Germany is at a pivotal moment for its long-term economic outlook. Major investments in infrastructure, the energy transition and digitalization, including the government’s €500 billion public investment program, provide a timely opportunity to strengthen the country’s economic growth and competitiveness. Research[published today](https://www.iwkoeln.de/studien/valeria-quispe-alexander-burstedde-paula-risius-dirk-werner-wer-baut-die-zukunft-fachkraeftemangel-als-bremse-fuer-wachstum-und-investitionen-in-deutschland.html) by the German Economic Institute (IW) points to a critical obstacle: the country’s labor shortage, including almost 150,000 unfilled positions in skilled trades critical to the investment program, such as electricians, plumbers, heating, ventilation and air conditioning technicians, industrial maintenance workers and many others. IW estimates that labor shortages across all occupations cost Germany approximately €49 billion in forgone economic output in 2024 alone.


At the same time, too many young people struggle to access training opportunities that match their needs. More than 400,000 people aged 20 to 24 in Germany, representing 10% of that age group overall, were neither employed nor in education or training in 2025, up from 8.8% in 2022, according to Germany’s Federal Statistical Office.1


BlackRock Future Builders Germany will begin with an initial €5 million philanthropic commitment to two national organizations that support young people at two pivotal stages of the apprenticeship journey: entering training and successfully completing it. JOBLINGE helps young people secure apprenticeship and employment opportunities, while the Senior Expert Service’s (SES) VerAplus program provides one-to-one mentoring to help apprentices stay on track and see their training through to the end. Together, these organizations are expected to help more than 1,500 people enter and succeed in skilled trades careers over the next three years.


Of the total €15 million philanthropic commitment, the remaining €10 million will be deployed through partnerships with organizations across Germany that are helping to prepare the next generation of skilled workers, with the program aiming to reach more than 5,000 people in total over five years as it expands.


“Germany has enormous ambitions for what it wants to build, and realizing them will depend on having the skilled workers to make it happen. The country already has one of the world’s strongest vocational training systems, and we’re proud to make it the first in Europe to launch BlackRock Future Builders. We’re investing in organizations working within that system to help more people start apprenticeships, complete their training and build lasting careers.” **Larry Fink, Chairman and CEO of BlackRock**


“A country’s future is ultimately shaped by the futures its citizens are able to build for themselves. As a long-term investor in Germany on behalf of our clients, we believe strengthening that foundation is part of our responsibility here. For more than 30 years BlackRock has been part of Germany’s economic journey, and BlackRock Future Builders builds on that commitment. By expanding pathways into skilled careers, we can help more people secure a stake in the country’s growth.” **Dirk Schmitz, Country Head of Germany, Austria and Eastern Europe at BlackRock**


“Germany faces a double challenge: many young people struggle to find a good start in an apprenticeship or career, while companies are urgently searching for skilled talent at the same time. With the support of The BlackRock Foundation, we can address exactly this intersection. We want to inspire young people about careers in infrastructure, construction, mobility and energy, prepare them to be job-ready, and connect them with employers. But entering an apprenticeship is only part of it. Young people also need the chance to complete it successfully. This partnership allows us to connect career orientation and placement more closely with ongoing support throughout the apprenticeship itself.” **Kadim Tas, CEO, JOBLINGE**


“The challenges we’re now seeing in Germany’s training and labor market were already becoming clear years ago. That is when we decided to act, and since 2008 we have been supporting apprentices through our VerAplus mentoring program, with backing from both public and private partners. Having The BlackRock Foundation alongside us now gives us real confidence and makes us even stronger, and it is a strength we will pass on to young people, successful apprenticeship journeys and the skilled workforce of tomorrow.” **Marion Sodemann, Managing Director, Senior Expert Service (SES)**


#### **** About BlackRock


BlackRock’s purpose is to help more and more people experience financial well-being. As a fiduciary to investors and a leading provider of financial technology, we help millions of people build savings that serve them throughout their lives by making investing easier and more affordable. For additional information on BlackRock, please visit[www.blackrock.com/corporate](https://www.blackrock.com/corporate)


#### About The BlackRock Foundation


Guided by BlackRock’s purpose to help more and more people experience financial well-being, The BlackRock Foundation funds and partners with organizations that strengthen financial security by helping people earn, save and invest earlier, more often and for their futures.


#### About JOBLINGE


Since 2008, JOBLINGE has demonstrated how measurable social impact can be achieved at the transition from school to work. Supported by a network of more than 3,000 corporate partners and thousands of volunteers, the initiative helps young people on their path into vocational training. More than 80% of participants in the JOBLINGE program successfully transition into working life with the support of JOBLINGE’s experts. Further information can be found at[www.JOBLINGE.de/en](https://joblinge.de/en/)


#### About Senior Expert Service (SES)


The Senior Expert Service (SES) is Germany’s largest organization for deploying volunteer experts and senior executives who are either retired or taking a professional sabbatical (World Service 30+). SES is headquartered in Bonn and has 16 offices across Germany, as well as 200 representatives in 90 countries worldwide. SES currently has more than 14,000 registered experts, bringing specialist knowledge from over 50 industries. Since its founding in 1983, SES has carried out more than 70,000 voluntary assignments in 170 countries. SES is supported by Germany’s leading business associations: the Federation of German Industries (BDI), the Confederation of German Employers’ Associations (BDA), the German Chamber of Commerce and Industry (DIHK), and the German Confederation of Skilled Crafts (ZDH). The Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) supports SES’s international activities, while the Federal Ministry of Education, Family Affairs, Senior Citizens, Women and Youth (BMBFSFJ) supports its work with apprentices in Germany. Further information is available at[www.ses-bonn.de](https://ses-bonn.de/home)
